extracted.intended_audience: students and readers of political philosophy/classics (readers of Plato's Republic)
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and normative guidance for selecting, educating, and testing philosopher-rulers and guardians in the ideal state (as argued in Plato's Republic). Focuses on required qualities, staged education, probations/tests, and the epistemic standard (knowledge of the Good).

rubrics_metrics.name: Philosopher's natural gifts (quickness, memory, courage, magnificence)
rubrics_metrics.description: "remember what we were saying of him, that he was to have quickness and memory and courage and magnificence—these were admitted by us to be the true philosopher’s gifts."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The philosopher/guardian should possess these natural endowments; they make him 'first among all' in youth and attractive to others. These qualities are prerequisites for the higher education and leadership roles, but by themselves can be misused if ill-educated or corrupted by honours and flatterers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Danger of diversion by honours, riches, and social flattery
rubrics_metrics.description: Those who excel in the philosopher’s gifts may be drawn away: "his friends and fellow-citizens will want to use him... Falling at his feet, they will make requests to him and do him honour and flatter him... Will he not be full of boundless aspirations... and dilate and elevate himself in the fulness of vain pomp and senseless pride?"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection and education must anticipate social pressures: without proper formation, even the best natures will be diverted from philosophy into vanity, politics, or corruption. Safeguards and rigorous training are needed to preserve the philosophic calling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guardians must be tested by pleasures and pains (patriotism probations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Guardians are to be "lovers of their country, tried by the test of pleasures and pains, and neither in hardships, nor in dangers, nor at any other critical moment were to lose their patriotism—he was to be rejected who failed, but he who always came forth pure, like gold tried in the refiner’s fire, was to be made a ruler."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Moral and motivational testing under stress is required: candidates must demonstrate steadfastness, loyalty, and incorruptibility under hardships and temptations. Failure is grounds for rejection; those who pass receive honours and office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Staged education: bodily training in youth, 'gymnastics of the soul' as intellect matures, then free study
rubrics_metrics.description: "In childhood and youth their study, and what philosophy they learn, should be suited to their tender years: during this period... the chief and special care should be given to their bodies... as life advances and the intellect begins to mature, let them increase the gymnastics of the soul; but when the strength of our citizens fails... then let them range at will and engage in no serious labour."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The curriculum is sequenced: early emphasis on physical formation and appropriate simple studies; gradual intensification of intellectual education (moral, musical, mathematical, dialectical) as maturity arrives; retirement from active duties when bodily strength wanes to allow contemplative freedom.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement of dialectic/higher knowledge (knowledge of the Good)
rubrics_metrics.description: "The guardian then... must be required to take the longer circuit, and toil at learning as well as at gymnastics, or he will never reach the highest knowledge of all... the idea of good is the highest knowledge... that of the good we know so little; and, without which, any other knowledge or possession of any kind will profit us nothing."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beyond practical virtues, guardians must pursue dialectic and grasp the Form/idea of the Good. This highest epistemic attainment is treated as essential: without knowledge of the Good, one cannot reliably know justice, temperance, or govern rightly. Education must therefore include rigorous training in dialectic and abstract principle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise in many kinds of knowledge to test soul's endurance
rubrics_metrics.description: "The aspirant must... be exercised also in many kinds of knowledge, to see whether the soul will be able to endure the highest of all, or will faint under them..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intellectual probations should expose candidates to diverse disciplines and increasingly difficult studies to determine whether their souls can bear the pressure of highest inquiry; inability to endure indicates unsuitability for the highest offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combination of quick intelligence and steadfastness required (rare conjunction)
rubrics_metrics.description: "quick intelligence, memory, sagacity, cleverness... and at the same time high-spirited and magnanimous... On the other hand, those steadfast natures... are apt to yawn and go to sleep over any intellectual toil... yet both qualities were necessary... they are mostly found in shreds and patches."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection requires a rare conjunction: agility of mind plus stability of character. Candidates lacking either (overly impulsive/intellectual but unsteady, or steady but torpid intellectually) are inadequate. The system must identify and cultivate those few individuals who combine both.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject pretenders who make persons, not things, their theme (avoid sophisms)
rubrics_metrics.description: "the harsh feeling which the many entertain towards philosophy originates in the pretenders... those who rush in uninvited... who make persons instead of things the theme of their conversation?... And when persons who are unworthy of education approach philosophy... what sort of ideas and opinions are likely to be generated? Will they not be sophisms captivating to the ear, having nothing in them genuine..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Educational and institutional filters must exclude opportunistic or craft-trained individuals whose motives are status or rhetoric; otherwise philosophy is polluted by sophistry and mere appearances. Authentic education focuses on truth and things (ideas), not personal aggrandizement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lawgivers/designers must model constitutions on absolute justice/beauty/temperance
rubrics_metrics.description: "They will begin by taking the State and the manners of men, from which... they will rub out the picture, and leave a clean surface... they will first look at absolute justice and beauty and temperance, and again at the human copy; and will mingle and temper the various elements of life into the image of a man... And one feature they will erase, and another they will put in, until they have made the ways of men, as far as possible, agreeable to the ways of God."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Constitution-design is an artistic, iterative process that uses the transcendent Forms (justice, beauty, temperance) as the model. Lawmakers should not legislate until they have an ideal template and then reshape society step-by-step to approximate that ideal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Educational aim: move souls from opinion (visible world) to knowledge (intelligible world)
rubrics_metrics.description: Discussion of the divided line and the sun-analogy: distinctions between "the many" (visible, opinion) and "the absolute" (ideas, knowledge); sight needs light (sun) as the soul needs the Good to see truth; "the soul... when resting upon that on which truth and being shine, the soul perceives and understands... but when turned towards the twilight of becoming and perishing... she has opinion only."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pedagogy should cultivate the capacity to progress from sensory-based opinion to intellectual understanding, teaching students to rely on principles rather than images or hypotheses. The ultimate pedagogical aim is acquaintance with the Good as the source of truth and being.
